newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds closed on the upside on Monday with the long term future contract at a new high of 112.24.
But dealers were wary of profit-taking later this week.
"We expect some kind of correction this week," said Alfredo Urrutia, economist at Societe Generale in Madrid. He added that Tuesday and Wednesday's bond auctions could trigger selling.

Earlier the Spanish Treasury announced that t expected to sell tomorrow between 275 and 350 billion pesetas in three- and 10-year bonds, while on Wednesday it will offer between 225 and 250 billion pesetas in five- and 15-year bonds.
Spanish Treasury is to offer tomorrow a new 10-year bond, with a lower coupon of 7.35 percent. The benchmark 8.80 percent coupon closed today at 112.72 versus 111.80 on Friday, yielding 6.90 percent.
It broke the seven percent level on Friday for the first time ever.

On the domestic side dealers will focus tomorrow on the Bank of Spain's regular reporchase tender, which is widely expected to see the key money rate unchanged. A Reuter poll among 10 financial experts showed no-one expects an official rate cut tomorrow, but eight out of ten forecast it by the year-end.
But the Spanish market should move mainly in line with other European bonds, especially Bunds.

"This week we should see a string of data, which could show some improvement in the German economy," said Robert Huw, strategist at Natwest in London. This should push down bonos too, he said. Germany is due to publish November industrial production, and third quarter GDP.
The 10-year spread over Bunds was trading at around 131 basis points, almost unchanged from Friday's close.
"We'd expect it to widen above 140-145 basis points" said SocGen's Urrutia.
Taking no notice that the Italian lira was nearly at two-and-a-half-year high against a generally weaker mark, the peseta was little moved from its Friday level trading at 84.25/4.27 per mark.
